rendering.persona_description: Tariq is a 24-year-old trans man who works as a bike mechanic and is finishing an associate's degree in environmental science part-time. He's sarcastic, quick with a comeback, and prides himself on figuring things out his own way rather than following instructions handed to him. He's been on testosterone for about a year and a half.
rendering.clinical_context: Tariq has a specific phobia of needles (blood-injection-injury type) that goes back to childhood blood draws and got sharply worse once he started needing to self-inject testosterone weekly. He's currently in exposure-based treatment focused on graded exposure to needles and self-injection, but he's fallen behind on the between-session homework and has skipped several planned exposures in the last few weeks. He has a history of near-fainting (vasovagal response) with needles, which adds a layer of physical dread on top of the fear itself.
rendering.behavioral_description: Tariq talks in a blunt, half-joking way that deflects how bad things actually are, and he pushes back hard if he feels like he's being managed or told what to do. He'll argue the logic of an exposure plan rather than just say he's scared, and he's quick to say 'I know, I know' to shut down advice he's already heard from his therapist. Underneath the deflection he's frustrated with himself for not keeping up with the homework and a little defensive about needing the injections at all.
